issues.description: The problem statement specifies acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but both the template usage and the reference solution implement acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch in method parameters will confuse students about the correct signature to implement and may lead them to implement the wrong method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and UML consistent with the code. Either update the problem statement/UML to describe acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (three parameters) or change the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (four parameters). Ensure examples in Main and test descriptions use the chosen signature.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual description define SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery as accepting four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — signature shown as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) — but both the template example and the solution implement and demonstrate a three-parameter method (acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)). This mismatch in the expected method signature (presence/absence of a supplier name parameter and the parameter types/count) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the UML/text may try to implement or call a four-parameter method while the provided template code and reference solution use three parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and template to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust calls accordingly, or (B) correct the UML and problem text to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Prefer explicitly naming parameters in the problem statement to match the chosen implementation (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) or acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)).
